heroLead: Gentle, restorative 1:1 sessions of easy movement, breathwork, and rest for people living with PCOS or PCOD, built around how you feel each week. Practised alongside the care your doctor provides.
empathyLabel: You don't have to do this alone
empathyText: PCOS looks different for everyone: irregular cycles, deep tiredness, weight that is hard to shift, skin and mood changes. Yoga can be a steady, soothing part of your week that supports rest, calm, and an active routine alongside your doctor's care.
helpsH2: How yoga can support life with PCOS.
helpsSubhead: Four gentle levers, working together. None of them is a treatment. All of them are habits you can keep.

levers.title: An active routine you can keep
levers.body: Regular, gentle movement supports an active routine and a healthy weight, which many doctors recommend as part of living with PCOS. We keep it enjoyable so it sticks.

levers.title: Calmer, steadier days
levers.body: When stress runs high, slow breathing, meditation, and guided relaxation help you feel more settled and even from one day to the next.

levers.title: Comfort through your cycle
levers.body: Hip- and abdomen-friendly poses, traditionally used to help you feel more comfortable through cramps, bloating, and tension, adapted to where you are in your cycle.

levers.title: Rest that restores
levers.body: Yoga nidra and supported rest for the tiredness and broken sleep that often come with PCOS, so you wind down properly and rest more deeply.

howH2: How we work with you to get there.
howSubhead: One teacher who knows your name and your goals, not a different face every week.

steps.title: We get to know you
steps.body: A relaxed first session: your energy, your cycle, what your doctor has suggested, and anything to adapt for.

steps.title: A plan shaped to you

steps.title: Guided live 1:1s

steps.title: We grow it gently

whoForText: Anyone diagnosed with PCOS or PCOD, or who has been told their cycles are irregular, who wants a gentle, consistent practice to support an active routine, rest, and a sense of steadiness alongside their doctor's plan.

faqs.q: Can yoga treat or cure PCOS?
faqs.a: No. Yoga supports rest, calm, and an active routine alongside the care your doctor provides. It isn't a treatment for PCOS or any other condition, and you shouldn't change medication without your doctor.

faqs.q: Can yoga help me lose weight with PCOS?
faqs.a: Regular, gentle movement supports an active routine, which is part of what many doctors recommend. We never promise a weight result, and we scale every session to your fitness and energy that day.

faqs.q: How is this different from your hormonal health sessions?
faqs.a: The hormonal health page covers cycle changes, perimenopause, and menopause in general. This page is shaped around PCOS specifically: the pacing, the poses we lean on, and the questions people ask.

faqs.q: Can I practise during my period?
faqs.a: Yes, gently. Tell your teacher and we'll adapt, often leaving out strong inversions if you prefer.

faqs.q: I'm trying to conceive. Is this still suitable?
faqs.a: Gentle yoga is generally fine, but tell your teacher and keep your doctor in the loop. If you become pregnant, we switch to a pregnancy-safe approach and ask for your doctor or midwife's clearance first.

faqs.q: How soon might I notice anything?
faqs.a: Everyone is different. Many people first notice calmer stress, steadier energy, and better sleep, and consistency helps the most.

safetyTitle: Yoga supports your care, it doesn't replace it
safetyText: These sessions support your overall wellbeing and are practised alongside professional medical care. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Please tell your teacher about any conditions or symptoms so they can adapt your session safely, and keep your doctor in the loop.
